## Professional Summary

Data Scientist with 14+ years building and owning predictive models and advanced analytics in SQL, R, and Python across regulated data environments in higher education and national security, plus commercial product development. Own and extend the enrollment prediction framework behind the highest-rated product at a higher-ed analytics firm, reaching 1% MAPE and 59 NPS across 80 users. Delivered two LLM-powered products from prototype to general availability in six months using RAG and custom Python. Co-created the data visualization standards covering research figures and business dashboards, adopted by 28% of a 14,000-person workforce.

## Technical skills

**Programming:** R, Python, SQL, AI-Assisted Development (Claude Code), MATLAB, SAS\

**LLM:** RAG, Pinecone, OpenAI API & Vector Store, Embeddings, Prompt Engineering, LLM-as-Judge Calibration, Golden Datasets\

**Machine Learning:** Scikit-Learn, Predictive Modeling, Model Validation, Feature Engineering, Applied Statistics, Experimental Design, A/B Testing\

**Visualization:** R Shiny, ggplot2, Tableau\

**Data & Infrastructure:** AWS, Docker, Git, CI/CD Pipelines, R Package Development, Data Virtualization (Denodo, Tibco), Spark\

## Professional Experience

**Data Scientist,** *Capture Higher Ed,* Louisville, KY, 08/2022--Present\
Designed, implemented, and maintained internal- and partner-facing predictive models in R, Python, and SQL on AWS for a higher education enrollment management and marketing firm. Adapted predictions to institutions of differing size and geography through feature engineering and external data sources including census and school performance data. Enabled Customer Success and education advisors to apply model output to client enrollment strategy, and partnered with 9-12 client institutions to define how each counts enrollment, reconciling those definitions to a common internal standard so predictions stayed comparable across schools.

-   Assumed sole ownership of the enrollment prediction framework and codebase after its original author departed, extending it to become the company's highest-rated product at 59 NPS across 80 users, with MAPE narrowing from 10% six months out to 1% by May.
-   Scoped 2 LLM-powered products with senior leadership, Product, Engineering, and Infrastructure, translating product requirements into technical approach and delivering both to general availability within a 6-month deadline, with an evaluation framework combining human graders, LLM-as-judge calibrated against human scores, and golden-dataset automated scoring.
-   Found that students visiting campus before applying enroll at near-certainty, redirecting client recruitment spend away from students already converting toward segments where outreach changes the outcome.
-   Engineered R Shiny application automating model validation across the data science team's full book of 15-20 higher education clients, defining absolute, percent, and raw error measures across 15 prediction points and 5 models, replacing 3 manual checkpoints and surfacing seasonal patterns through exploratory analysis that improved subsequent predictions.
-   Consolidated scattered R scripts into main package infrastructure as a reusable analytical system, eliminating a single-person bottleneck so all 4 team members could generate client onboarding reports and reducing generation time from 2 days to 4 hours.
-   Recognized company-wide by peer vote for first-year impact, selected from 21 candidates across two hiring years (Rookie of the Year, 2023).
-  Assumed ownership of containerized development environment supporting the 4-person data science team's production model deployment, implementing ARM architecture support to enable migration to faster machines and maintaining annual security updates for R/Python libraries and federal data sources.

Built and deployed interactive applications for 2 predictive models and 4 data visualizations supporting safety, security, and employee retention at a federally funded national security laboratory. Delivered analysis to leadership on the performance of the $177.7 million Laboratory Directed Research & Development (LDRD) program. Streamlined access and data quality for 83 enterprise data sets using SQL and data virtualization (Denodo, Tibco) to join sources across systems into unified data streams, and established research software practices by documenting CI/CD pipelines in Docker and GitLab. -   Won competitive CIO funding (1 of 3 from ~20 proposals) to co-develop the enterprise data visualization style guide for research figures and business dashboards, achieving 28% adoption across a 14,000-person workforce as measured by website analytics.
-   Rebuilt the interface for ASSURE for Safety, the laboratory's safety risk model, partnering with a separate data sciences organization and a UX researcher to replace a legacy .NET implementation with 4,714 lines of R in a deployed R Shiny application that showed managers which organizations faced elevated incident risk and which indicators drove it, validated through two rounds of usability testing.
-   Co-led the 5-person data visualization sub-team supporting a department portfolio of 50+ Tableau and 20+ Shiny visualizations; served as technical lead for the separate 4-person UI/UX data visualization style guide team.
-   Authored 3 internally used R packages as reusable analytical systems, standardizing database connections, plotting defaults, and package management.
-   Evaluated Tableau against R Shiny for enterprise visualization delivery, comparing cost, licensing, version control, and customization, and presented the findings to IT staff across the national laboratory system.
